Transmission Control Protocol
Introduction



                            1.  INTRODUCTION

The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is intended for use as a highly
reliable host-to-host protocol.

1.1.  Motivation

TCP is a connection-oriented, end-to-end reliable protocol designed to
fit into a layered hierarchy of protocols which support multi-network
applications.  This paragraph continues across a page



                                                                [Page 1]


                                                          September 1981
Transmission Control Protocol
Introduction



break and finishes here.

                     3.  FUNCTIONAL SPECIFICATION

The connection states are described here.

3.9.  Event Processing

The processing depicted in this section is an example.

  1.  CLOSED                                               LISTEN

  2.  SYN-SENT    --> <SEQ=100><CTL=SYN>               --> SYN-RECEIVED

  3.  ESTABLISHED <-- <SEQ=300><ACK=101><CTL=SYN,ACK>  <-- SYN-RECEIVED

The steps above complete the connection.
